config.title: Buffer & encoding

intro.title: Buffer & encoding
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple program that creates and manipulates binary data using Node.js Buffers. You'll learn the core concept of encoding, which is how text is converted to and from binary data for storage or transmission. The main technologies involved are the Node.js Buffer class and common character encodings like UTF-8. By the end, you'll understand how to create buffers from strings, read their contents, and handle different encoding formats in your applications.
intro.usecase: Buffers and encoding are fundamental when handling binary data in Node.js applications, such as processing file uploads in web forms or APIs. For example, when users upload images or documents through a dashboard interface, Node.js uses buffers to temporarily store this binary data before saving it to disk or processing it further. Developers also rely on encoding conversions when reading configuration files, parsing network protocols, or working with databases that store binary data. Understanding buffers is crucial for building efficient file processing systems, streaming services, or any application that deals with raw data beyond plain text.

objectives: Initialize a Buffer from a string using a specified encoding
Convert a Buffer to a string using a different encoding
Manipulate binary data within a Buffer by reading and writing individual bytes
Apply Buffer methods to concatenate multiple Buffer instances into a single Buffer
Integrate Buffer operations with file system functions to read and write binary data
Configure a Buffer to allocate a specific size and fill it with data
Control encoding and decoding processes to handle text data across different character sets

steps.title: Create a function to demonstrate creating buffers
steps.instruction: Create a function named createBuffers() that demonstrates three different Buffer creation methods: Buffer.from(), Buffer.alloc(), and Buffer.allocUnsafe(). The function should return an object containing these three buffers.
steps.hint: Define a function that creates buffers using the three methods and returns them in an object. You can use arrow function syntax or function declaration.

// Create a function named createBuffers() that demonstrates Buffer.from(), Buffer.alloc(), and Buffer.allocUnsafe() methods
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named createBuffers is created that returns an object with three different buffers.
successCriteria: The createBuffers function exists and returns an object with buffers created using Buffer.from(), Buffer.alloc(), and Buffer.allocUnsafe().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function returns an object containing all three buffers created with the different methods.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function doesn't seem to be implemented correctly. Remember to create buffers using Buffer.from(), Buffer.alloc(), and Buffer.allocUnsafe() and return them in an object.

steps.title: Initialize a buffer from a string
steps.instruction: Inside your createBuffers() function, create a buffer from the string 'Hello' using Buffer.from() and assign it to a variable named stringBuffer.
steps.hint: Use Buffer.from('Hello') to create a buffer from the string. Remember to store it in a variable so you can use it later.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a buffer from a string
const myBuffer = Buffer.from('Example text');
steps.expectedOutcome: The createBuffers() function will now have a stringBuffer variable containing a buffer created from the string 'Hello'.
successCriteria: A variable named stringBuffer is declared inside createBuffers() and assigned the result of Buffer.from('Hello').
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using Buffer.from('Hello') and assigning it to a variable named stringBuffer inside the createBuffers() function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside createBuffers(), create a variable called stringBuffer and assign it Buffer.from('Hello').

steps.title: Create a buffer with specific encoding
steps.instruction: Inside the createBuffers function, add another buffer creation using Buffer.from('Hello', 'utf8') to explicitly specify UTF-8 encoding. Store it in a variable named bufferWithEncoding.
steps.hint: Use Buffer.from() with two arguments: the string and the encoding type. The encoding 'utf8' is the default, but we're specifying it explicitly for learning purposes.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a buffer with explicit encoding
const myBuffer = Buffer.from('Hello', 'utf8');
steps.expectedOutcome: The createBuffers function will now have a buffer created with explicit UTF-8 encoding, demonstrating how to specify character encoding when creating buffers.
successCriteria: A buffer variable named bufferWithEncoding is created using Buffer.from('Hello', 'utf8') inside the createBuffers function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using Buffer.from() with both the string and encoding arguments, and storing it in a variable named bufferWithEncoding.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside createBuffers(), use Buffer.from('Hello', 'utf8') to create a buffer with explicit UTF-8 encoding and store it in bufferWithEncoding.

steps.expectedOutcome: The createBuffers function now includes a bufferAlloc variable storing a 10-byte zero-initialized buffer.
successCriteria: A variable named bufferAlloc is declared and assigned Buffer.alloc(10) inside the createBuffers function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.instruction: Inside the manipulateBuffer function, after writing 'Node' to the buffer, read the buffer content back as a string using buffer.toString() and store it in a variable named readString.
steps.hint: Use the toString() method on the buffer variable you created. You can call it without arguments to get the default UTF-8 string representation.
steps.expectedOutcome: The manipulateBuffer function will now be able to extract the written string data from the buffer.
successCriteria: The manipulateBuffer function contains a variable named readString that stores the result of calling toString() on the buffer.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
